properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 14 at 6:51PM CDT until September 15 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 110 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Portions southeast Arkansas, northeast Louisiana, and
central Mississippi.

* WHEN...From 11 AM to 7 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat related
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Anchorage
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued September 14 at 3:49PM AKDT until September 16 at 12:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...South to southeast winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts of up to 40
to 50 mph expected.

* WHERE...Anchorage.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Tuesday to noon AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result. Trees are still mostly green and fully
leafed, causing them to be more vulnerable to damage from the
strong winds.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A strong fall storm system moving into the
western coast of Alaska will produce a prolonged period of strong
and gusty winds across the Anchorage area.  Winds will initially
develop out of the southeast on Tuesday morning as strong winds
along the Turnagain Arm bend into town.  The strongest winds will
be focused on the south and west side of town until winds turn out
of the south and spread into the rest of the Anchorage Bowl Tuesday
afternoon.  Winds will then slowly diminish through Wednesday
morning.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Kuskokwim Valley
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 14 at 3:36PM AKDT until September 18 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Upper Kuskokwim Valley. This
includes the cities of McGrath, Nikolai, And Takotna.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...The Kuskokwim River is currently at bankfull. Soils
remain moist and excessive runoff may result in localized flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain is forecasted to begin Monday afternoon. Rain should
continue through Wednesday morning with storm total rainfall
expected to be around 1 to 2 inches. Minor pooling/ponding of
water in low-lying and flood prone areas is possible with the
already saturated ground conditions beginning on Tuesday. Small
stream and creek flooding is possible as we expect very high
water levels throughout the week in response to the heavy rain.

- The Kuskokwim River dropped below bankfull Monday morning.
River levels are expected to rise again in response to the heavy
rain beginning Monday afternoon and remain high through the rest
of the week.

- We will continue to monitor the situation closely and update as
necessary.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared to take
action should flooding develop.

Soils remain moist and excessive runoff may result in flooding of
rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

properties.areaDesc: Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 14 at 3:36PM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. More rain is expected beginning
Tuesday and will continue through Wednesday afternoon. Storm
total rainfall during this time will be around 0.50" to 1.00". It
has been very wet lately and this amount of rain has the
potential to bring the Chena and Little Chena Rivers above minor
flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc

- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 14 at 3:13PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* This (Monday) evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest
rainfall expected late Tuesday morning through Tuesday night.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna may reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

At 712 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a gust front, capable of
producing winds to around 30 knots. This gust front was located along
a line extending from Figure Eight Island to near Dallas Rock to 9 nm
northeast of Wr2, moving southwest at 15 knots.

Locations impacted include...
10 Mile Boxcars, Liberty Ship, Dallas Rock, Billy Murrell Reef, Buoy
Off Carolina Beach, Masonboro Sea Buoy, Dredge Wreck, Harris Reef, 5
Mile Boxcars, 10 Mile Rocks, School House Reef, and North Masonboro
Island.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots and locally
higher waves. Boaters in small craft should consider seeking safe
harbor immediately until this gust front passes. If caught on the
open water, prepare for deteriorating conditions. Make sure you and
your crew are wearing properly fitted life jackets.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 14 at 3:44PM MST until September 14 at 6:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Apache County in northeastern Arizona...

* Until 645 PM MST.

* At 344 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area, east of Highway 191 east and
northeast of Saint Johns. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Apache County.

This includes Highway 191 161 between mile markers 323 and 334.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Zui River, Jarvis Wash and Carrizo Wash.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 6:45 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 6:45 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 4:44PM MDT until September 14 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...West Central Hudspeth County in western Texas...

* WHEN...Until 745 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 444 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Acala.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.headline: Wildfire with IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for the west side of Atoka Reservoir.
properties.description: At 1715  a large and destructive wildfire was burning out of control north of Atoka  spreading rapidly north along the west side of the Atoka Reservoir. Never drive into heavy smoke.

Northwestern Pitkin County in west central Colorado...

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 3:40PM MDT until September 14 at 6:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Sierra County in south central New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 645 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 338 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has
fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Caballo Lake.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 645 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 14 at 12:50PM MST until September 14 at 11:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Southeast Arizona, including the following
areas, Catalina and Rincon Mountains, Chiricahua Mountains, Dragoon
and Mule and Huachuca and Santa Rita Mountains, Eastern Cochise
County below 5000 feet, Galiuro and Pinaleno Mountains, South
Central Pinal County, Southeast Pinal County, Tucson Metro Area,
Upper Gila River Valley, Upper San Pedro River Valley and Upper
Santa Cruz River Valley/Altar Valley.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Well above normal moisture levels for September are expected to
result in scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms capable
of producing heavy rainfall today. Rain totals of 1 to 2 inches
are expected with the stronger storms with isolated amounts over
2 inches possible. Areas that received substantial rainfall over
the past 72 hours will be more susceptible to flash flooding.
This rainfall will result in faster response in washes, creeks,
and storm drainages.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 109.

* WHERE...Coastal Galveston, Coastal Harris, and Inland Galveston
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 7 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tampa Bay Ruskin has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Elevated water levels are expected along the river over the next
several days due to recent heavy rainfall.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM EDT Monday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.

properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside by staying hydrated, wearing
lightweight and loose fitting clothing, and limiting strenuous
activities to the early morning or evening. Check up on relatives and
neighbors. Never leave young children or pets in an enclosed vehicle,
even for a short time, as temperatures can quickly rise to
life-threatening levels.

reduce risk when outdoors, the occupational safety and health
administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in shaded
or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat should be

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 14 at 8:26AM AKDT until September 16 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels as high as 1.5 to 4.0 feet above the normal
highest tide line. Southwest winds 35 to 45 mph with gusts up
to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kwigillingok,
Kongiganak, Kipnuk, Toksook Bay, and Tununak.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Monday to 10 PM Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal flooding of low lying areas and erosion are
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The previously issued High Surf Advisory
has been replaced with this Coastal Flood Advisory. A rapidly
deepening, broad low pressure system centered west of the
Pribilof Islands is on track to send a strong corridor of 25 to
35 mph south to southwest winds towards the Kuskokwim Delta
Coast by early this afternoon. Winds quickly increase this
evening and overnight to 35 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph
expected. Coinciding with 2 high tide cycles, water levels along
the Kuskokwim Delta Coast will be up to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. As the low makes progress northward Tuesday
morning, winds will maintain their magnitude but shift to out
of the west, which will raise water levels for Toksook Bay and
Tununak up to 4 feet above the normal high tide line as well.
Conditions will begin to improve Wednesday morning as the low
exits the region. Additionally, periods of moderate to heavy
rainfall will compound coastal impacts for the advisory
duration.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* Monday evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest rainfall
expected through Tuesday evening.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna will likely reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 109 expected.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Limestone, Madison, Morgan, Colbert, Franklin
AL, Lauderdale, and Lawrence Counties. In Tennessee, Lincoln and
Moore Counties.

* WHEN...From 11 AM to 8 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In Central WY Fire Zones...280...283...289...300.
In Southwest WY Fire Zone....279.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central WY...Fremont...Natrona.
In Southwest WY...Sweetwater.

* IMPACTS: Low Humidities and Strong Gusty Winds could cause
erratic fire behavior.

* WIND: West 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 10 to 15 percent.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now....or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds...low relative humidity...and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.
